page: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64gb is a memory-optimized server from the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is limited to a 1 GB network-attached volume, and there are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations generally fall into the average tier. Text processing is highly efficient, scoring in the top 10% on Geekbench, while medium-sized LLM prompt processing shows weaker relative performance.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a cost-effective allocation of memory relative to compute cores, making it suitable for memory-bound tasks that do not require massive parallel processing. However, the lack of substantial local storage means workloads requiring high-speed local disk I/O must rely on external network storage, which introduces potential latency tradeoffs.

This configuration is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, text processing pipelines, and lightweight web serving. It is also capable of handling software compilation and small-scale language model text generation, though it is not designed for heavy parallel computing or GPU-accelerated tasks.
